programmes.d: After an Arkansas state trooper is shot and killed, officers catch the murderer.
A woman and her infant son vanish. The husband is frantic. The clues are scarce, but hopes linger, even as the hours and days tick by without a word. Was she on the run, or the victim of foul play?
In 1992, a Washington, DC professor was shot and killed as she tried to get into her car.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Cracking The Cartel
programmes.d: A mother and child are kidnapped, a bystander is murdered. Violence such as this shattered a quiet Texas neighborhood and exposed a drug cartel that flourished where it was least expected.
Cuban detainees in Atlanta revolt in response to their impending deportation.

In Arizona, an armored van loaded with cash failed to reach its destination. Authorities suspected an inside job. When the vehicle was recovered with the drivers and the cash missing, those suspicions grew even more.
A nocturnal killer preys on senior citizens in 1997 Louisiana.

Over a thousand hunting accidents are reported in the United States each year. Fewer than ten percent of them are fatal. But when one hunter's death seemed suspicious, the FBI was called in to investigate.
In 1996, a series of bank robberies in Texas baffled authorities.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Above the Law
programmes.d: California Highway Patrolman George Gwaltney discovered the body of 23-year-old Robin Bishop near her car on a remote desert highway.
Two masked bandits rob armored-car couriers at Las Vegas casinos.

In 1995, our nation's capital was also our nation's murder capital. Even the police weren't safe. While Washington, DC, law enforcement targeted criminals, the criminals targeted law enforcement, even gunning down officers on patrol.
In 1997, two men used a sledgehammer to break into a Camden, New Jersey home.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Held For Ransom
programmes.d: Wealth has its rewards, but it also brings its dangers. Kidnapping is one of them. No ordeal is more horrifying for a family than to have a child taken.
Investigative techniques.

When a family was murdered in Arkansas, it seemed like an isolated event. But soon the crime was revealed to be part of an ever-widening circle of violence that defined a new age of domestic terrorism.
Croatians seek to secure Croatia's sovereignty via terrorism.
When three people were found murdered in their home, it appeared like a burglary gone awry. But a crime this horrific deserved a closer look.
In 1994, men dressed as police officers commit a plague of home robberies in Detroit.

Two armed bank robbers hit a Seattle bank taking over 150,000 dollars. Before they can escape police confront them and the pair splits up. As authorities search block by block they learn one was a career criminal with a long history of violence.
The FBI captures five terrorists who tried to hijack a Royal Jordanian flight in 1985.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Melissa Brannen: Missing
programmes.d: In 1989, residents of a close-knit apartment community in Virginia gathered for a holiday celebration. For Tammy Brannen and five-year-old daughter Melissa, Christmas was always a special time. Then, without warning, the little girl was gone.
The Cuban nationalist group Omega 7 takes credit for a murder.

A Chicago street gang thought they had figured out how to kidnap people for ransom again and again, and never get caught. But their one mistake was they underestimated the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
The investigation of a New York City bombing that cost a young officer his eye.
In Langley, Virginia, a terrorist fired into rush hour traffic. The victims seemed randomly selected, but the motive appeared to be political, targeting employees of the Central Intelligence Agency.
In 1990s Philadelphia, a ruthless grab for power led to a full-scale mob war.
In the 1970's and 80s, people went to Alaska looking for a fresh start, to reinvent themselves, or to disappear for a while. Some of those disappearances weren't by choice.
In the late 1980s, the FBI matched wits with a cunning bank robber known as the Shootist.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: The Coffee Shop Murders
programmes.d: At a coffee shop in Washington, DC, three employees were shot to death. Evidence at the crime scene pointed in many different directions. Was this a hate crime, a robbery gone wrong or an act of cold-blooded vengeance?
The Los Macheteros terrorist organization sought to end U.S. rule of Puerto Rico through violence.

In a city awash in narcotics the drug lords have all the power even over the police. Corruption in New Orleans grew like cancer, eating away at public safety and threatening to destroy the city. Crooked cops break the laws they were sworn to uphold.
In the mid-1980s, as drug profits grew, gangs ruled the streets of Chicago.

Willow Springs, Illinois, seemed like any other quiet Midwestern community. But it was really one of the most corrupt places in the nation. This tiny village, nestled just outside of Chicago, was in the hip pocket of organized crime.
A car bomb kills Orlando Letelier.

Power is a responsibility as well as a privilege. But in the wrong hands, power can corrupt. For former Deputy Attorney General for the State of Delaware, losing sight of his sworn oath to uphold justice could prove lethal.
A copy machine, placed in a busy Las Vegas casino, is actually a bomb.

In the 1980's, two partners created a nightclub that would bring them wealth and international fame. The male strip club phenomenon promised female patrons fun and excitement. But the bright lights hid a dark side.
A special task force was formed in the early 1990s to combat the flow of Colombia cocaine.
In June of 1997, a crime wave swept Iowa like a tornado. It left a trail of robbery, kidnapping, and murder in its wake, and then it moved on. No one knew where.
Authorities sought to put two ruthless drug kingpins behind bars for their crimes.

A businessman went to Florida to make one last deal before he retired-he never returned home to his millions. Authorities examined who was closest to him and who stood to gain from his disappearance. But this time conventional rules didn't apply.
The FBI investigated corruption among the detectives of the San Juan, Puerto Rico Police Department.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Cat and Mouse
programmes.d: He was a predator, abducting girls and young women from their own front yards in broad daylight. He was a sadist: phoning one victim's family, taunting them, boosting then dashing their hope, and he wouldn't stop until we stopped him.
An 80-year-old woman is found barely conscious next to the body of her murdered son.

Drops of blood and a torn screen were all that's left to tell authorities what happened to a woman in Indiana. The 21 yr. old victim was taken from her home on a spring morning. She appeared to have no real enemies, there was no clear motive.
Notorious bank robber Byron Chubbuck escaped from New Mexico State Penitentiary in 2000.
